pitch: Rare, unpredictable events shape history, markets and our lives—and we are poorly equipped to see them coming.
br: The bell curve, great intellectual fraud
very safe · very risky · nothing in between
quiz: What are the three features of a black swan?
Rare, extreme in impact, explained after the fact
It also depends on what the observer knows.
What does the turkey story illustrate?
The past doesn't guarantee the future, and confidence can peak at the moment of danger
A thousand reassuring days said nothing about the decisive day.
What is the difference between Mediocristan and Extremistan?
In the first, no single case changes the average; in the second, one can dominate everything
Height belongs to the first, wealth to the second.
What does Taleb hold against the bell curve?
It underestimates extreme events in many domains
Turning chance into a coherent story and believing you understand the past
The more detailed a story, the more credible it seems—and the less probable it is.
What does the story of sailors who prayed and survived illustrate?
Silent evidence: we forget those who prayed and drowned
Being very cautious with the essentials and very bold with a small share
Avoid the false comfort of the middle.
What does Taleb recommend in the face of the unpredictable?
Reduce your exposure to severe consequences and keep margins
